specific_issue: Headway staggering on overlapping bus corridors requires driver duty and layover re-rostering under industrial fatigue rules.
evidence_anchor: Bus Safety Act 2009 (Vic); Bus Industry Award 2020
strongest_counterargument: Existing driver breaks and fatigue requirements do not inherently prevent shifting departures by 15 minutes; rosters and layovers can be rescheduled within contractual variation frameworks.
falsifier_criterion: Depot vehicle-block and driver-duty scheduling demonstrating that a 15-minute headway shift fits within compliant rosters without additional vehicle or driver requirements.
verdict_impact: Reclassifies C08 from zero-cost claim to valid scheduling improvement with operational rostering and contract variation dependencies.

specific_issue: Offsetting bus departure times to space overlapping local routes breaks timed rail transfers at Melton Station.
evidence_anchor: PTV Melton Line Timetable; GTFS feed
affected_cohort: Commuters connecting to V/Line rail services
strongest_counterargument: In outer suburban networks, rail connectivity takes precedence over local trunk spacing; staggering must preserve transfer synchronisation.
falsifier_criterion: GTFS connection model showing 10-minute headway offset maintains <10-minute transfer window to all peak and off-peak trains.
verdict_impact: Requires qualification of C07/C08 to balance local corridor spacing against rail transfer penalties.

specific_issue: Imposing stringent 15-minute lead times and door-to-door delivery on FlexiRide exposes microtransit geometric cost failure ($35-$50 per trip).
evidence_anchor: Currie (2018); DTP FlexiRide trial data; policies.json
affected_cohort: Outer-suburban on-demand riders, fixed-route bus users, DTP contract managers
strongest_counterargument: Imposing stringent minimum service standards is an intentional policy mechanism designed to expose the poor economics of microtransit and justify replacing it with efficient fixed-route buses; transition is managed via transparent costing and operational decision frameworks without requiring statutory triggers.
falsifier_criterion: DTP operational data showing microtransit maintains per-passenger subsidies below scheduled fixed-route benchmarks under 15-minute response standards.
verdict_impact: Reclassifies C11/C12 from contradiction to deliberate policy mechanism with operational transition framework (no statutory triggers required).

specific_issue: Rigid 1km distance guarantee incentivises urban sprawl and forces buses into circuitous, low-frequency loops.
affected_cohort: Transit riders seeking competitive travel times; fringe developments
strongest_counterargument: Coverage mandates dilute service frequency on direct arterial routes, depressing ridership and encouraging driving.
falsifier_criterion: Spatial network model demonstrating that 1km coverage standard can be delivered without reducing trunk route frequencies.
verdict_impact: Downgrades 1km guarantee from rigid standard to flexible design caution C05.

specific_issue: Direct grid reallocation leaves 10-15% of outer suburban residents in curvilinear estates beyond safe walking distance.
affected_cohort: Elderly and mobility-restricted residents in curvilinear street layouts
strongest_counterargument: Grid corridors benefit arterial commuters while stranding residents who cannot walk 800m to the nearest arterial road.
falsifier_criterion: Pedestrian access audit proving all residential dwellings in estate have direct, safe access to grid stops.
verdict_impact: Identifies distributional trade-offs and walking access limitations in C03.

specific_issue: Multi-billion capital rail electrification creates fiscal borrowing competition with recurrent operational bus service hours.
evidence_anchor: Victorian Budget 2026-27 BP2; DTF debt projections
affected_cohort: Outer suburban bus riders; regional commuters
strongest_counterargument: Capital borrowing locks up state fiscal capacity under a $178B debt load, creating trade-offs with recurrent bus service hours.
falsifier_criterion: Budget papers showing separate dedicated funding lines for bus operations that are legally insulated from capital mega-project borrowing ceilings.
verdict_impact: Identifies capital-versus-recurrent budget sequencing and prioritization tension.

specific_issue: Charging outer station car parks before feeder bus networks exist imposes an inequitable burden on transit-dependent workers.
affected_cohort: Outer suburban commuters without local bus access
strongest_counterargument: In the absence of frequent feeder buses, parking fees act as a regressive burden on outer suburban commuters rather than a modal shift incentive.
falsifier_criterion: Evidence that station parking charges in growth areas induce modal shift to buses rather than highway driving or economic exclusion.
verdict_impact: Requires explicit geographic boundaries (inner commercial parking vs outer rail park-and-ride exemptions).

specific_issue: Franchise margin auditing and clawbacks must be separated from operator compensation for new service hours.
evidence_anchor: Transport Integration Act 2010; Bus Contract Reforms
strongest_counterargument: Auditing unearned margin at contract renewal is distinct from compensating operators for newly commissioned revenue service hours.
falsifier_criterion: Contract mechanisms demonstrating clear distinction between margin clawback on existing contracts and fair unit rates for new service kilometres.
verdict_impact: Separates franchise profit auditing from service variation contracting mechanics.

specific_issue: Broad untargeted cash arrears grants achieve lower crisis efficiency than screening for formal VCAT possession listings.
evidence_anchor: Shinn et al. (2013); Evans et al. (2016)
strongest_counterargument: While grants provide broad stabilization across poverty dimensions, screening for formal court notices maximizes crisis diversion efficiency.
falsifier_criterion: Causal evaluation showing untargeted grants prevent shelter entry at comparable cost-efficiency to screened eviction diversion.
verdict_impact: Down-rates Option 1 / A02 from well supported to qualified (shelter entry is one metric among broader housing stability value).

specific_issue: Unconditional state rent arrears payouts risk landlord subsidy capture and subsequent non-renewal at lease end.
evidence_anchor: Pawson et al. (2024); VCAT annual reports
strongest_counterargument: Landlords can accept state arrears payments and still issue non-renewal notices without statutory 6-month lease extension conditions.
falsifier_criterion: Tenancy sustainment longitudinal data showing >80% lease extension rates without formal lease conditions.
verdict_impact: Confirms landlord capture risk in A07 and supports mandatory lease extension conditions.

specific_issue: One-off cash grants fail to sustain tenancies when rent structurally exceeds 50% of household income.
strongest_counterargument: Temporary liquidity relief cannot overcome structural ongoing income deficits, resulting in recurrent churn.
falsifier_criterion: Peer-reviewed evidence of 24-month housing retention following one-off grants among households paying >50% income in rent.
verdict_impact: Reclassifies Option 1 / A02 as weak mechanism for chronic structural poverty without ongoing subsidies.

specific_issue: VCAT repayment orders under s 330A risk severe hardship and secondary default for deeply impoverished households.
evidence_anchor: RTA 1997 s 330A, s 91ZM; Greiner et al. (2013)
affected_cohort: Low-income tenants on statutory income support
strongest_counterargument: Enforcing repayment plans on unviable incomes risks nutritional deprivation and secondary eviction under s 91ZM.
falsifier_criterion: VCAT compliance data showing >70% completion of arrears repayment plans by households on statutory benefits without material hardship.
verdict_impact: Identifies repayment hardship risk in A03 and need for hardship waivers.

specific_issue: Relying on VCAT duty lawyers creates procedural bottlenecks under existing tribunal listing delays and unrepresented rates.
affected_cohort: Unrepresented renters in regional and outer suburban VCAT venues
strongest_counterargument: Tribunal backlogs and legal aid workforce constraints limit physical duty lawyer coverage to a fraction of possession hearings.
falsifier_criterion: Registry data showing universal representation achieved at VCAT residential tenancies list without hearing delays.
verdict_impact: Identifies procedural capacity barrier in A03 requiring pre-tribunal community mediation.

specific_issue: Market-rate upzoning around railway stations risks accelerating redevelopment and displacement of older low-rent private flats.
evidence_anchor: Liu et al. (2022); Collinson et al. (2023)
affected_cohort: Existing private renters in station precincts
strongest_counterargument: Unconditional upzoning risks demolishing older affordable low-rise stock before aggregate market supply expands over multi-year horizons.
falsifier_criterion: Study proving private transit-oriented development does not displace low-income renters in Australian metropolitan corridors.
verdict_impact: Presents policy options for deliberation (inclusionary zoning, public land development, tenant right-of-return).

specific_issue: Social housing transfer cannot serve as an immediate eviction diversion mechanism due to 17-month priority waitlists.
strongest_counterargument: Severe capital shortage (3% stock) makes social housing a long-term structural goal, not an agile crisis diversion tool.
falsifier_criterion: Demonstration of rapid social housing vacancies allocated to divert imminent private evictions within 14 days.
verdict_impact: Confirms supply bottleneck in Option 4 / A05.

specific_issue: Disbursing emergency arrears grants on joint tenancies without survivor-centred screening leaves domestic violence survivors legally and physically vulnerable.
strongest_counterargument: No adopted policy requires unsafe joint tenancies to be preserved; survivor-centred screening, confidential support, informed consent, and safe-exit pathways (including RTA s 91V) are operational safeguards for research proposal F-113, not a contradiction in adopted policy; lease severance must not be mandatory or automatic.
falsifier_criterion: Evaluation protocols demonstrating tenancy sustainment grants achieve survivor safety without dedicated risk assessment and confidential consent.
verdict_impact: Reclassifies A07 from policy contradiction to essential intervention design safeguard in research proposal F-113 (emphasizing survivor choice and consent).

specific_issue: Averted crisis costs (hospital and justice congestion) are non-cashable economic benefits, not Treasury cash dividends.
evidence_anchor: Victorian Budget 2026-27 BP2; DTF VGR Guidelines; RoGS (2025)
strongest_counterargument: Adopted policies do not claim downstream hospital savings as cashable Treasury revenue; this was an analytical overstatement in F-113.
falsifier_criterion: Victorian Treasury guidelines confirming societal benefit-cost gains cannot be used as cash offsets against recurrent program budgets.
verdict_impact: Corrects F-113 claim A08 from policy contradiction to research evidence rating correction (RC09).

specific_issue: Adopted policy platform completely omits health, family violence, climate adaptation, and child protection.
strongest_counterargument: Fusion 41 adopted policies concentrate heavily in transport and governance while omitting 70%+ of state budget responsibilities.
falsifier_criterion: Identification of adopted Victorian platform policies in health, domestic violence, or climate adaptation.
verdict_impact: Identifies structural platform omission F18.

specific_issue: Scoring housing tractability at 4/5 overstates state jurisdictional control relative to federal macroeconomic levers.
strongest_counterargument: Housing is macroeconomically constrained under state levers (federal tax, interest rates), distorting ranking.
falsifier_criterion: Sensitivity analysis showing ranking stability when tractability is scored at 2/5 or 3/5.
verdict_impact: Re-evaluates ranking robustness F19.

specific_issue: Separating housing instability (VP-001) from family violence (VP-002) ignores that domestic violence drives 43% of female homelessness.
affected_cohort: Women and children facing violence and housing churn
strongest_counterargument: Siloed problem framing evaluates generic rent arrears while deferring survivor safety and perpetrator exclusion.
falsifier_criterion: Data proving female homelessness can be effectively halved without dedicated family violence intervention.
verdict_impact: Corrects siloed problem framing F20.

specific_issue: Universal basic cash dividends compete with targeted crisis relief for scarce state fiscal resources.
affected_cohort: Low-income households in acute crisis; Treasury
strongest_counterargument: Distributing broad cash payments leaves fewer resources for intensive, targeted crisis support.
falsifier_criterion: State macro-fiscal model proving universal dividend can be funded alongside targeted emergency brokerage.
verdict_impact: Identifies fiscal prioritisation trade-off F23.

specific_issue: Deliberative citizen juries operate within statewide planning baselines per Key Point 2 carve-out.
strongest_counterargument: Operative text already specifies citizen assemblies cannot block compliant housing or override statewide codes.
falsifier_criterion: Statutory drafting codifying non-derogable planning baselines in deliberative democracy instruments.
verdict_impact: Acknowledge existing policy carve-out; recommend codification F24.

specific_issue: Dividend is explicitly conditional on audited distributable surplus after debt service and capital preservation.
strongest_counterargument: Policy explicitly conditions dividends on net surplus after debt service, maintenance and reserves; no immediate payment from debt.
falsifier_criterion: Audit showing fund investment yields consistently and safely exceed state cost of borrowing.
verdict_impact: Acknowledge explicit policy conditionality (dividends paid only from audited net surplus after debt service).

specific_issue: Open government presumption and proactive document disclosure are robustly evidence-supported.
strongest_counterargument: Reduces public sector corruption and improves policy accountability at negligible net operational cost.
falsifier_criterion: Peer-reviewed evidence that open disclosure harms government administrative efficiency.
verdict_impact: Explicitly records verified strength F26.

specific_issue: Sunday scheduled departure clustering on Brooklyn Road (Routes 457/459) is an indisputable timetable fact.
strongest_counterargument: Buses scheduled 2 minutes apart followed by 58-minute gaps is mathematically verified in official GTFS timetables.
falsifier_criterion: PTV GTFS publication showing staggered 30-minute headways on Brooklyn Road.
verdict_impact: Explicitly records verified schedule fact F27.
